subject: Bridgecrest hosting constraints & deployment asks
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Arianna Lopez <arianna.lopez@bridgecrest.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@bridgecrest.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Bridgecrest hosting constraints & deployment asks

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clarity on the regulatory drivers and the S3/egress constraints. This thread is a short recap + concrete asks so we can scope a Private (VPC/on-prem) POC for Bridgecrest.

Key pain & goals we heard
- Data residency: all client PHI must remain in Bridgecrest-controlled networks (no persistent egress permitted).
- Regulatory driver: state-level healthcare regulator requires demonstrable isolation and the ability to audit KMS access.
- Operational constraint: TechOps cannot open inbound tunnels to vendor-managed control planes; any management plane access must be customer-initiated (pull model) or via air-gapped install.
- Performance: low-latency inference (<120ms p95 for 512-token requests) for triage workflows.

Technical constraints we captured
1) No outbound connections from production subnet to third-party control planes unless through an approved NAT + proxy.
2) HSM/KMS keys must be customer-managed; Redwood needs to support key wrapping with your KMS.
3) All logs containing request-ids must be retained on-prem for 90 days and available via S3-compatible storage inside the VPC.
4) Installation may need an air-gapped bundle (pre-signed packages + hardware USB key for validators) if vendor connectivity is disallowed.

Immediate asks / next steps (owners)
- Arianna / TechOps: please send the network diagram and firewall rule summary (egress / ingress) we discussed — we need CIDR ranges and proxy hostnames for the install matrix. (deliverable: bridgecrest_network_requirements.xlsx) — due Tue 12/8.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare an install matrix showing options: VPC-only (peered control plane), private control plane (customer-hosted), and fully air-gapped appliance. Include rough timelines and effort estimates. (deliverable: redwood_private_install_matrix.pdf) — due Wed 12/9.
- Redwood (Ben): draft a limited SOW for a 6-week POC including acceptance criteria and success metrics (latency, throughput, auditability). (deliverable: sow_draft_bridgecrest_v1.docx) — due Fri 12/11.

Constraints & risks to flag
- If TechOps requires a fully air-gapped install, our standard hosted telemetry and automatic security patching paths are limited — we will need offline patch bundles and a monthly sync cadence.
- KMS integration timeline depends on bridgecrest security sign-off for cross-account key policies; that can add 2–3 weeks.

I’ve attached a template for the network details and the quick checklist we use for air-gap installs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up with TechOps next week.

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Arianna Lopez <arianna.lopez@bridgecrest.com>

Cc: TechOps <techops@bridgecrest.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@bridgecrest.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bridgecrest hosting constraints & deployment asks

Priyom — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from TechOps (copied):

- Network: we cannot whitelist third-party control plane IPs permanently. We can either: (a) provide a temporary outbound-only ephemeral tunnel for install and updates, or (b) accept an air-gapped install with offline patching.
- KMS: Bridgecrest uses a centralized HSM in our PCI boundary. We will provide a key-wrapping API endpoint that is only callable from within the VPC.
- Logging: we need all request-level logs to be written to a customer-owned S3 bucket in our account — no hosted log aggregation in Redwood.

I've attached the network diagram export and firewall rule list (filled). Note: we've redacted a couple of CIDRs for privacy in this mail, full file is in the Drive link.

Next best times for a TechOps
- Mon 12/8 10:00–11:00 PT (tech deep-dive)
- Tue 12/9 14:00–15:00 PT (architecture review)

A few asks back to Redwood:
1) Can you confirm whether the POC can run entirely within our VPC with no outbound control-plane egress? If not, provide the minimal control-plane endpoints needed.
2) For an air-gapped install, do you support an install validator (USB token) and offline patch bundles?

Thanks — attaching: bridgecrest_network_requirements.xlsx, firewall_rules_redacted.csv

Regards,
Arianna Lopez
Senior Infrastructure Manager | Bridgecrest Health
arianna.lopez@bridgecrest.com

Attachments: bridgecrest_network_requirements.xlsx, firewall_rules_redacted.csv

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Arianna's reply and the attached network sheet. Action items for Redwood team before the Mon tech session: 

1) Marissa: build two short docs (1) "VPC-only deployment (no-control-plane-egress) — what resources Redwood requires inside the VPC and the customer-managed services we expect" and (2) "Air-gapped install process" including packager/validator flow and monthly patch cadence. Keep docs <3 pages each.
2) Ben: draft a POC acceptance criteria doc with measurable tests: p95 latency for 512 token requests, throughput for 20 concurrent sessions, and log delivery verification to S3.
3) I will confirm internal legal about the SOW language for offline/airgap responsibilities and get back by EOD Fri 12/11.

Notes from the attached network file (high level):
- They have a managed NAT/proxy in the DMZ; installation must originate from a jump-host inside the production VPC.
- KMS endpoints are private; any key-wrap calls will need to be routed inside the VPC.

Let's aim to have the two docs + POC criteria in my drive folder by EOD Sun 12/6 so I can review.

--
Priyom

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Bridgecrest hosting constraints & deployment asks

Arianna — quick confirmation. We can support two POC flavors:

A) VPC-local deployment (preferred): Redwood components run inside your VPC (EC2/GKE). Control-plane endpoints are optional — we will provide a small health/metrics collector that can be deployed as a customer-managed sidecar. No persistent outbound egress required.

B) Air-gapped appliance: full offline install bundle + USB-based install validator. Patches are delivered as signed bundles; Bridgecrest engineer will pull and apply updates on a monthly cadence. Telemetry is written to your customer-owned S3 and never sent to Redwood unless you opt in.

Next steps I will own:
- Share the 2-page VPC deployment checklist and the air-gap install brief by EOD Sun 12/6. (Marissa will deliver the docs into the Drive link above.)
- Schedule TechOps deep-dive Mon 12/8 10:00 PT — booking invite to follow.

If that aligns, I'll proceed with the SOW draft for the 6-week POC and include both deployment options and a switch-over plan.

Best,
